official.deadline_note: The 15 January 2027 deadline is the first admission round application deadline at University Admissions, which controls scholarship eligibility. The scholarship application itself opens only on the day students receive the Notification of Selection Results (1 April for master's, autumn 2027 intake) and stays open a few days; in the 2026 round it ran 26-30 March (closed 23:59 CET on 30 March). LiU lists the LiU Scholarship application period for the current cycle as TBD.
official.application_cycle: Autumn 2027 intake - applications open 16 October 2026, close 15 January 2027; documents and application fee due 1 February 2027; master's Notification of Selection Results 1 April 2027; autumn semester starts August 2027
official.status_note: LiU's degree-studies page shows applications for the autumn 2027 intake open 16 October 2026 with a 15 January 2027 deadline. The 2026 scholarship round has concluded (recipients published 10 April 2026) and the next scholarship window is listed as TBD.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'The tuition fees for a student awarded a LiU International Scholarship are normally reduced by 50%' and, in the rules, 'The scholarship covers the total tuition fee or part of the tuition fee. If the scholarship covers part of the tuition fee, the student must pay the remainder of the fee no later than the payment deadline.' LiU's tuition-payment guidance refers to partial awards of 25-75%.
benefits: Tuition fees for a student awarded a LiU International Scholarship are normally reduced by 50% (partial awards of 25-75% per LiU's tuition-payment guidance)
The scholarship is valid for the specific year and master's programme stated in the Notification of Selection Results
For master's students, the fee/scholarship normally covers a workload of 30 credits per semester as long as the courses are included in the programme
Holders who pass at least 75% of their courses in the first academic year receive the scholarship for the following academic year
eligibility: You applied for a master's programme at Linköping University by the deadline for the first admission round
You submitted all the required documents by the deadline
You chose a master's programme at Linköping University as your first priority (ranked as number 1 of 4)
You have been admitted to your first choice in the First Notification of Selection Results (usually end of March)
You are required to pay tuition fees

New for 2026: you meet the minimum academic standard - GPA of 3.5 or higher on a 4.0 scale, a first or high second class degree, or an equivalent average (typically 75% or above in India, 80-85% or above in China, or 8.0/10 or above on a 10-point CGPA scale)
requirements: Applications which do not meet the minimum academic standards will not be considered
Eligible students are invited to apply by email before the deadline for applications closes
No additional documents are needed to support your application

Scholarship holders must pass at least 75% of their courses during the first academic year to receive the scholarship for the following academic year (only results registered on 1 July count; e.g. 45 of 60 credits by 1 July)
documents: No additional documents are needed to support the scholarship application - eligibility is assessed from the admission application and the Notification of Selection Results (underlying admission documents are due by the 1 February documentation deadline)
selection_criteria: Minimum academic standard: GPA of 3.5 or higher on a 4.0 scale, a first or high second class degree, or an equivalent average
Institutional rankings will be considered as part of the evaluation process

Linköping University reserves the right to determine internally, year by year, how many scholarships will be offered, what percentage will be offered and the merit process once eligibility has been met and if there are more applicants than scholarships available
coverage: The scholarship covers the total tuition fee or part of the tuition fee (normally a 50% reduction; partial awards of 25-75%)
For master's students the fee/scholarship normally covers a workload of 30 credits per semester; any additional courses beyond 30 credits carry an additional fee
Tuition fees do not cover course literature, housing costs or living expenses - LiU states you need approximately SEK 10,000 a month for such expenses
application_method: Apply for a master's programme at Linköping University through University Admissions (universityadmissions.se) in the first admission round, paying the SEK 900 application fee and submitting all required documents by the deadlines
Eligible admitted students are invited to apply for the scholarship by email; the application opens on the day the Notification of Selection Results is published and is only open for a short window
No additional documents are needed to support the scholarship application
official.application_route: Apply to a LiU master's programme via universityadmissions.se by 15 January; if admitted to your first choice in the first notification round, apply for the scholarship via the emailed invitation in the short window that follows.
official.study_mode: Full-time - LiU master's programmes are normally two years / 120 ECTS and the fee/scholarship covers a 30-credit workload per semester
official.citizenship_residency: The applicant must be a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland and be required to pay tuition fees; if the status changes to that of a non-fee-payer the scholarship is no longer valid and LiU must be informed in writing
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is aimed at international master's degree students who are required to pay tuition fees (citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland)
official.duration: The specific year and master's programme stated in the Notification of Selection Results; normally a 30-credit workload per semester, with programmes typically two years / 120 ECTS
official.description: The LiU International Scholarship is a limited number of tuition-fee reductions awarded by Linköping University to new international master's students with significant academic potential who are required to pay tuition fees; the tuition fees of an awardee are normally reduced by 50%. Since 2026 only applicants who meet a minimum academic standard (GPA 3.5 or higher on a 4.0 scale, or an equivalent average) are considered, and institutional rankings form part of the evaluation.
official.program_type: University-administered partial tuition-fee scholarship for fee-paying international master's students
official.english_requirement: The scholarship sets no separate English test; eligibility rests on the master's entry requirement, English 6 / English Level 2 equivalent: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no section below 5.5, TOEFL iBT total 90 with writing 20 (results to 20 Jan 2026) or total 4.5 on the 1-6 scale with no section below 4 (results from 21 Jan 2026), or PTE Academic 62 (writing 61); 60 ECTS taught in English from listed countries can also meet it

not_confirmed: Scholarship application window dates for the 2027 cycle (LiU lists the LiU Scholarship application period as TBD; the 26-30 March dates published on the page belong to the 2026 round)
Tuition fee amounts - LiU directs applicants to the individual programme pages or universityadmissions.se for specific fees, so no single published figure applies to this percentage-based award
verification.notes: Scholarship terms (normally 50% tuition reduction, 2026 minimum academic standard, 2026 window 26-30 March, renewal/rescission rules, 25-75% partial awards) read directly from liu.se; current cycle dates from LiU's degree-studies page and universityadmissions.se (first admissions round is the round specifically for international students); English requirement from universityadmissions.se since the scholarship has no separate test. The brief's official_source_url liu.se/en/education/scholarships returns 404 - the live official page is liu.se/en/article/scholarships. No fixed monetary amount is published: the award is a percentage of the programme's tuition fee.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a tuition discount, not a study grant: LiU itself estimates about SEK 10,000 a month for living costs that no part of this scholarship touches. The real decision happens months before the scholarship window opens - your January application, your document deadline, and ranking a LiU programme first are what make you eligible. When the invitation email arrives after the 1 April notification you must respond within days, but you will not need to prepare any extra documents. Weigh it against the Swedish Institute scholarship, because winning an SI award cancels the LiU one.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Fee-paying master's applicants with strong grades (GPA 3.5/4.0 or the 75-85% country equivalents) who genuinely rank LiU first and can self-fund living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply via universityadmissions.se in the first admissions round by 15 January and rank a LiU master's programme as number 1 of 4
Pay the SEK 900 application fee and upload every supporting document by 1 February - late documents make you ineligible regardless of grades
Verify your GPA converts clearly to the published thresholds; institutional ranking feeds the evaluation, so make your institution recognisable
Watch your email and universityadmissions account from 1 April: the scholarship window opens on results day and closes within days
Budget the remaining tuition plus roughly SEK 10,000 per month, and plan to pay tuition by 15 May so the residence permit can be processed
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 1 February document deadline - all required documents must be in by then to be considered
Ranking LiU second or lower, or not being admitted to the first choice in the First Notification of Selection Results
Falling below the GPA 3.5/4.0 or country-equivalent bar - such applications are explicitly not considered
More eligible applicants than awards: LiU decides internally how many scholarships and at what percentage, so meeting every rule still guarantees nothing
Losing year-two funding by completing under 75% of first-year credits by the 1 July assessment date
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining 25-75% of the programme tuition fee, living costs estimated by LiU at approximately SEK 10,000 per month, course literature, housing, and travel to Sweden - none of which this award covers
document_audit: The scholarship application itself needs no documents, but the admission application it rides on does - a missing transcript makes you ineligible before the scholarship is even considered
Your transcript must visibly support the claimed GPA; with institutional rankings factored into evaluation, an obscure or poorly documented institution can weigh against you
Recipients must attach LiU's published recipient-list PDF to their Swedish Migration Agency residence-permit application
alerts: The window is measured in days (26-30 March in the 2026 round) and the 2027 dates are still TBD - if the invitation email is missed, the chance is gone
Winning a Swedish Institute scholarship rescinds the LiU award automatically
Failure to obtain a residence permit in time for registration rescinds the scholarship; pay tuition early - the 15 May deadline applies to March/April offers
The award is tied to one specific programme and year from the Notification of Selection Results and can be revoked, e.g. for suspension from studies
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application at universityadmissions.se closes 15 January; fee and documents due 1 February; master's results land 1 April; an emailed invitation then opens a several-day scholarship application with no supporting documents.
